prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for every homeowner — the best one for you depends on budget, project size, timeline, color/finish needs, and how much prep or repair is required. I can, however, help you find a top option by giving the criteria to look for, the questions to ask, and next steps to get a short list of highly rated local painters.

What to look for
- Strong local reviews on Google, Yelp, Houzz and/or Angi; consistent 4+ star ratings and recent jobs.
- Proof of insurance (general liability and workers’ comp) and any required local business license.
- Portfolio of completed interior jobs similar to yours (photos and references).
- Clear written estimate that breaks out labor, paint, materials, surface prep, repairs, number of coats, and cleanup.
- Written contract with scope, start and completion dates, payment schedule, warranty/guarantee.
- Good communication and a responsible project manager/foreperson on-site.
- Color consultation availability and use of quality paint brands (e.g., Benjamin Moore, Sherwin-Williams) if that matters to you.

Red flags
- No insurance or unwillingness to provide proof.
- Lowball estimate without a written scope or a request for full payment up front.
- Vague timeline, no references, or poor communication.
- Painters who skip prep (no patching/sanding/taping) or won’t agree on a finish/coat count.

Questions to ask every company
- Are you insured and can you provide a certificate?
- Do you have references from recent interior painting jobs?
- How do you handle surface prep and repairs?
- Which paint brands and sheen will you use and why?
- How many coats are included? Is primer included?
- What’s your timeline and payment schedule?
- Do you provide a written warranty?

Getting estimates
- Get 3 written estimates. Compare them by scope, not just price.
- Ask each company to show similar completed work and provide references you can call.

If you’d like, I can:
- Pull together a vetted short list of 3–5 top-rated interior painters in St. Louis (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood), or
- Help you draft an email/phone script to request estimates and ask the right questions.

Which would you prefer? Provide your ZIP code and any details (size of job, number of rooms, ceilings, trim, budget) and I’ll take the next step.
